Start here

ai-agent-lib gives every LangGraph agent and MCP server the same governed plumbing: who the caller is, what they may do, a record of what happened, content checks, a model chosen by configuration, and data reached only through named queries. Teams write the graph and the tools. The library hands back ordinary LangGraph and LangChain objects that happen to be governed.

Ten minutes from an empty folder to a tested agent and MCP server, with no cloud account. <lib> is your checkout of the repository.

uv run --project <lib> --package ai-agent-lib-cli agentlib init payments-ai --owner payments
cd payments-ai
uv sync --all-packages
uv run agentlib new mcp directory --description "The people directory"
uv run agentlib new agent helper --description "Answers questions about people" --mcp directory
uv sync --all-packages
uv run pytest                      # the generated tests, offline
uv run agentlib check              # the whole gate CI runs
uv run agentlib doctor             # checks every service against its .env
uv run agentlib run directory      # terminal 1: the MCP server
uv run helper "Who is in the payments team?"   # terminal 2: the agent

Then read on in this order: the core idea for the mental model, the worked example for the code you just generated, configuration to switch adapters, and the testing, observability and evals chapters before you go to production. When something fails, when something goes wrong explains the error you are reading. The reference lists every variable, option and flag with its default.

The core idea spec §1–2

An agent's business logic is small. What makes it hard to ship in an enterprise is the ring of concerns around every model call and every tool call: identity, authorisation, audit, content safety, data access rules, observability, configuration per environment. Each team used to solve these again, differently. ai-agent-lib solves them once, behind interfaces, and lets each environment choose how.

Five promises

  • Native LangGraph. No graph DSL. You write StateGraph code; five calls into the library make it governed.
  • One code path from laptop to Fargate. Environment variables choose an adapter for each concern. Local and server-side adapters mix freely, so you can run the real Bedrock model against local files and rules.
  • Testable by injection. Every dependency is injected. Unit tests need no network, no cloud account and no wall-clock time.
  • Fail closed. A policy, audit or guardrail failure stops the request. Nothing quietly degrades to a fallback.
  • AWS first, portable later. Other clouds arrive as separate packages that pass the same contract tests.

The design principles

Eleven rules apply to every module. Most are enforced by tests in tests/architecture, so they hold as the code grows.

PrincipleWhat it means for youEnforced by
Ports and adaptersEach capability is a typing.Protocol in contracts. You depend on the port, never on Firehose or OPA.import-linter
Depend on interfacesA component names the ports it needs in its constructor.review, mypy
Constructor injection onlyNo singletons, no service locator inside nodes, no import-time side effects. Your graph gets a ServiceContainer and nothing global.architecture tests
Change stays localEvery likely change has one owning module.containment tests
Configuration names live in one placeOnly config knows a variable name. Adapters receive typed options objects.test_config_containment.py
Configuration selects names, never codeEAP_AUDIT_PROVIDER=firehose picks a registered factory. No import paths in configuration.provider registry
Fixed interceptor orderOptions switch stages on or off; they cannot reorder audit, policy and guardrails.stage enums
Typed failuresA denial is PolicyDenied, never retried, never turned into a fallback.error taxonomy
Scope is a typeStores take a Scope, never a raw key, so tenant isolation is not a convention.types
Async firstUse ainvoke. Adapters are async end to end.review
Determinism by injectionTime, IDs and paths come from an injected Clock, IdGenerator and options.testing kit

What the library does not do

  • It is not an agent framework or a hosting platform. You own the graph topology, prompts and domain schemas.
  • It does not run a sign-in flow. The caller's identity provider issues tokens; the library verifies them and carries the verified identity.
  • It never loads code from configuration, and it provisions nothing itself: agentlib deploy writes Terraform that you review and apply.

Architecture and stack spec §3–7

Configuration is read once into a frozen ServiceConfig. A ServiceContainer builds one adapter per port from a trusted registry of factories, and hands your code governed LangGraph objects. Graph code never sees which adapter sits behind a port.

.env + environment→ConfigResolver→ServiceConfig→ServiceProviders→ServiceContainer→your graph / MCP server

Layers inside ai-agent-lib-core

contractsPorts (Protocols), value types (Principal, RequestContext, Scope, StructuredOutput), the error taxonomy. Imports nothing else from the library.
configThe binding table, profiles and the resolver. The only module that reads the environment.
pipelineInterceptors for audit, budget, identity, policy, registry, guardrails, framing, structured output and resilience, in a fixed order.
adaptersLocal adapters: JSONL audit, rules engine, static identity, JWT, OPA client, DuckDB over CSV, REST, SQLite, file registry, pattern guardrails.
diServiceProviders (port, name → factory), ServiceContainer (the facade you use), doctor.
integrationslanggraph (governed model, tools, checkpointer), mcp (server middleware, client), http (agent entry point, health, graceful shutdown).
observability · testing · evaluationJSON logs, error reports and OpenTelemetry setup; fakes, scripted replies and config loaders for tests; eval cases, scorers and reports, off the request path.

Import rules, enforced in CI

  • contracts imports nothing else from the library. config, pipeline and adapters import contracts only.
  • config is the only module that reads the environment.
  • integrations.langgraph is the only core module that imports LangGraph.
  • ai_agent_lib_core never imports boto3 or ai_agent_lib_aws.
  • Request-path modules never import the CLI or the evaluation package.
  • A provider pack imports only contracts and kit from core.

How a call is governed spec §8

Every model call and every tool call passes through a pipeline of interceptors. The order is fixed by an enum, so no option can put policy after the call or skip the audit. Solid boxes run today; dashed boxes are reserved positions for stages that are specified but not built yet.

Model pipeline

audit→deadline→budget→identity→policy→context→input guardrails→structured output→output guardrails→resilience→model

Tool pipeline

audit→deadline→budget→registry→policy→approval→input guardrails→idempotency→judge→framing→result guardrails→resilience→tool
  • Audit is outermost, so it records denials and failures from every stage inside it. If the record cannot be written the call fails with IntegrityError, even if the call itself succeeded.
  • Deadline bounds the whole call, every check included, by the caller's deadline. An answer that arrives after it, even from a step that blocked the event loop, is refused (PolicyDenied, reason deadline_exceeded) and audited, never returned.
  • Identity requires a RequestContext and refuses a caller past their deadline (PolicyDenied, reason deadline_exceeded).
  • Policy asks the policy decision point about model.route (the model alias) or tool.call. The rule that allowed it is written to the audit record as policy_reason_code.
  • Registry refuses a tool that is not registered for the agent, or whose live input schema no longer matches its pin.
  • Guardrails check prompts, replies, tool arguments and tool results for size and personal data, and tool results for prompt-injection markers. Each finding is flag (record it) or block (deny).
  • Framing wraps every tool result as untrusted data before the model sees it, which blunts injected instructions.
  • Structured output validates the reply against a schema inside the pipeline, so a malformed reply fails and is audited as failed.
  • Budget counts model calls, tool calls and tokens per request and stops a request that reaches its limit with BudgetExceeded, before the call is made. The count is kept per caller and per invocation: a request ID a caller sends correlates records but never shares a budget with another caller or another request.
  • Resilience sits next to the model or the tool: it gives each attempt a deadline and tries a transient failure again with growing, jittered waits, within the caller's deadline. No attempt outlasts that deadline: when it runs out the call is denied with deadline_exceeded, and no retry starts that the deadline leaves no time for. A tool is tried again only when it only reads. The audit record says how many attempts there were.

On an MCP server the same idea applies at the door: services.mcp_server_kwargs() installs middleware that verifies the token, checks the caller's agent against the registry, asks policy about tool.call, and applies data.query obligations such as masked columns and row limits to every query result.

Cross-cutting concerns spec §7, §18

Each concern has one port, a local adapter that needs no account, and a server-side adapter for AWS. You use the same API in both places; configuration picks the adapter. Local adapters marked local only refuse to start when EAP_DEPLOYMENT_ENV is dev or prod.

ConcernYou callLocalServerNotes
Identityservices.authenticate(token, application=, thread_id=)static local onlyjwtOAuth 2.0 access tokens; Entra ID preset. Another issuer must say how its application tokens differ from users' (service_tokens_are; see docs/identity.md). A missing token is the development identity locally and a refusal when deployed.
Delegation to MCP serversservices.mcp_tools(server)development tokensjwt + exchangeThe caller's token is exchanged for one bound to the server's audience (on-behalf-of or RFC 8693). It is never forwarded as is.

Specified but not built yet: per-tenant budgets and the pause switch, approvals, context bounding, runtime judges, idempotency keys, long-term memory, caching, token-by-token streaming, the router for agent teams, erasure and release admission. See what is built.

Configuration spec §5

Configuration is environment variables with the EAP_ prefix. Locally they come from the service's .env file; deployed, from the task definition. Your code never reads a variable: it receives a typed, frozen ServiceConfig.

How a value is resolved

  1. ServiceContainer.from_env() reads the process environment first, then .env. The environment wins, so a deployment or a shell can override any line of the file.
  2. An EAP_ variable the library does not know stops startup, with a suggestion: EAP_MODEL_PROVIDR (did you mean EAP_MODEL_PROVIDER?).
  3. EAP_PROFILE supplies a default adapter for every section. EAP_<SECTION>_PROVIDER overrides one section; EAP_<SECTION>_OPTIONS passes that adapter's options as JSON.
  4. Options are validated by the adapter's own Pydantic model. Unknown keys and wrong types stop startup.
  5. Relative paths in options resolve against the folder of the .env file, so a service runs the same from any working directory.
  6. The one-way guard runs last: outside local, a local-only adapter is refused, and inside ECS, Fargate or Lambda the deployment environment must be named.

Every adapter declares its options model, so all of them are checked before anything is built and every problem is reported at once. To see what an adapter takes, with types, defaults and meanings, ask the command line; --schema prints JSON Schema for an editor:

uv run agentlib config options                  # every port and its adapters
uv run agentlib config options audit firehose   # one adapter's options
uv run agentlib config options limits           # EAP_LIMITS: timeouts, retries, budgets

To see the result and where each value came from, with secrets masked:

uv run agentlib config explain helper

EAP_PROFILE              local
                           from default
EAP_MODEL_PROVIDER       fake
                           from variable EAP_MODEL_PROVIDER
EAP_AUDIT_PROVIDER       jsonl
                           from profile local
EAP_POLICY_OPTIONS       {"path": "../../policies/agentlib/rules/data.yaml"}
                           from variable EAP_POLICY_OPTIONS
...

Mixing local and server adapters

Profiles are only defaults, so any combination works on a laptop. A common one during development is the real model with everything else local:

# agents/helper/.env
EAP_PROFILE=local
EAP_MODEL_PROVIDER=bedrock
EAP_MODEL_ID=anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0   # a model your account enables
AWS_PROFILE=dev-sso
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
EAP_TLS_CA_BUNDLE=C:/certs/corp-root.pem                  # only if TLS is inspected

Or test your rules against a real OPA while the rest stays local:

EAP_POLICY_PROVIDER=opa
EAP_POLICY_OPTIONS={"url": "http://localhost:8181"}

A production task definition

EAP_PROFILE=aws
EAP_DEPLOYMENT_ENV=prod
EAP_MODEL_ID=anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0
EAP_MODEL_ALIASES={"fast": "anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"}
EAP_IDENTITY_OPTIONS={"preset": "entra", "tenant_id": "<tenant>", "audience": "api://helper",
                      "exchange": {"client_id": "<app id>"}}
EAP_TELEMETRY=opentelemetry
EAP_LIMITS={"model": {"timeout_seconds": 60}, "budget": {"tokens": 200000}}
EAP_AUDIT_OPTIONS={"stream": "eap-audit-prod"}
EAP_CHECKPOINT_OPTIONS={"host": "eap.cluster-xyz.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com", "database": "agents", "user": "helper"}
EAP_REGISTRY_OPTIONS={"bucket": "eap-registry-prod"}
EAP_POLICY_OPTIONS={"url": "http://localhost:8181"}
EAP_GUARDRAILS_OPTIONS={"guardrail_id": "gr-123", "guardrail_version": "3"}
EAP_SECRETS_OPTIONS={"prefix": "eap/helper/"}
AWS_REGION=us-east-1

You do not write this by hand: agentlib deploy helper writes a starting agents/helper/deploy.env, and turns it into the task's environment and its permissions. See deployment.

Model IDs above are examples; use the IDs and inference profiles your account has enabled. The full list of variables, with defaults, is in the reference.

Rule of thumb. Put structure in files (rules, registries, named queries) and environment-specific facts in variables (where the stream is, which tenant). The same rules file then runs in the local engine and in OPA, and the same SQL runs on DuckDB and Redshift.

Worked example: a people-directory agent

We build what Start here generated: an MCP server, directory, with a tool over a CSV of people, and an agent, helper, that calls it. Analysts may see names and teams but not email addresses; managers see everything. Every file shown is what agentlib writes today, trimmed only of comments.

  1. The workspace

    uv run --project <lib> --package ai-agent-lib-cli agentlib init payments-ai --owner payments
cd payments-ai && uv sync --all-packages

    A workspace holds every agent and MCP server of one team, with one registry/ (which agents and tools exist), one policies/agentlib/rules/data.yaml (who may do what) and one uv environment. agentlib.toml records the answers it was generated from, so agentlib init --answers agentlib.toml recreates it elsewhere.

  2. The MCP server: two touchpoints

    uv run agentlib new mcp directory --description "The people directory"
# or start from your own data:
#   --from-csv ./exports   --from-openapi ./api.yaml   --from-redshift sales --database dw
    # mcp-servers/directory/src/directory/server.py
def build_server(services: ServiceContainer) -> MCPServer[Any]:
    server: MCPServer[Any] = MCPServer(
        APPLICATION,
        instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
        **services.mcp_server_kwargs(SERVER_ID, application=APPLICATION),  # touchpoint 1
    )
    source = services.data_source(DATA_SOURCE)                             # touchpoint 2

    @server.tool(name="directory.people_by_team")
    async def people_by_team(team: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The people in one team: platform, payments or risk."""
        result = await source.query("people_by_team", {"team": team})
        return result.to_payload()

    return server

    Touchpoint 1 installs the governing middleware: token check, registry check, policy and audit for every tool call. Touchpoint 2 returns a data source by name; the tool runs a named query, never SQL from a caller. The query is a file with its contract in the header:

    -- queries/people_by_team.sql
-- description: The people in one team: platform, payments or risk.
-- param team: string
-- max_rows: 50
-- classification: confidential
SELECT person_id, name, team, email
FROM people
WHERE team = :team
ORDER BY person_id
    # mcp-servers/directory/.env
EAP_DATA_SOURCES={"people": {"kind": "duckdb_csv", "data_dir": "data", "queries_dir": "queries"}}
EAP_CHECKPOINT_PROVIDER=none
EAP_REGISTRY_OPTIONS={"agents_path": "../../registry/agents.yaml", "tools_path": "../../registry/mcp-tools.yaml"}
EAP_POLICY_OPTIONS={"path": "../../policies/agentlib/rules/data.yaml"}
EAP_IDENTITY_OPTIONS={"audience": "directory", "subject": "dev-user", "tenant": "dev-tenant", "roles": ["analyst"]}

    In production only the data source line changes: {"people": {"kind": "redshift_data", "queries_dir": "queries", "database": "dw", "workgroup": "analytics"}}. The SQL is the same file.

  3. The agent: five touchpoints

    uv run agentlib new agent helper --description "Answers questions about people" --mcp directory
    # agents/helper/src/helper/graph.py
async def registered_mcp_tools(services: ServiceContainer) -> list[BaseTool]:
    entry = services.registry.agents.get(APPLICATION)
    tools: list[BaseTool] = []
    for server in entry.mcp_servers if entry is not None else ():
        tools += await services.mcp_tools(server)                    # touchpoint 2
    return tools


def build_graph(services: ServiceContainer, mcp_tools: Sequence[BaseTool] = ()) -> CompiledStateGraph:
    tools = services.tools([greet], read_only=["greet"])             # touchpoint 1
    tools += mcp_tools
    model = services.model("default").bind_tools(tools)              # touchpoint 3

    async def agent(state: State) -> dict[str, list[AnyMessage]]:
        reply = await model.ainvoke([SystemMessage(SYSTEM_PROMPT), *state["messages"]])
        return {"messages": [reply]}

    builder = StateGraph(State, context_schema=RequestContext)
    builder.add_node("agent", agent)
    builder.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tools))
    builder.add_edge(START, "agent")
    builder.add_conditional_edges("agent", tools_condition)
    builder.add_edge("tools", "agent")
    return builder.compile(**services.compile_kwargs())              # touchpoint 4


async def answer(graph, services, context: RequestContext, question: str) -> str:
    result = await graph.ainvoke(
        {"messages": [HumanMessage(question)]},
        **services.invocation(context),                              # touchpoint 5
    )
    return str(result["messages"][-1].content)
    TouchpointWhat it adds
    1 services.tools()Your own functions as tools, each call through the tool pipeline: policy, guardrails, framing, audit.
    2 services.mcp_tools()The tools of a registered server, with a token exchanged for that server per call and pins checked.
    3 services.model()The model behind an alias, through the model pipeline. bind_tools and with_structured_output work as in LangChain.
    4 services.compile_kwargs()The configured checkpointer, with thread IDs scoped to the caller. A thread is read or written only for the caller the run's context names; outside a run, bind one with bind_request_context(context) before aget_state.
    5 services.invocation(context)The caller's RequestContext for this run, which every stage reads.

  4. Rules and registry

    Each new command appends the rules its service needs. The file is yours; agentlib never changes or removes a rule that is there. The first matching rule allows; no match denies. A document that breaks the schema (an unknown key, action or obligation, a duplicate id) denies every call with invalid_rules, rather than letting part of it through.

    # policies/agentlib/rules/data.yaml (excerpt)
schema: agentlib.rules/v1
rules:
  - id: directory-analysts-see-no-email
    actions: [data.query]
    applications: [directory]
    roles: [analyst]
    resources: ["people.*"]
    max_classification: confidential
    obligations:
      mask_columns: [email]
      max_rows: 50

  - id: helper-uses-its-models
    actions: [model.route]
    applications: [helper]
    resources: [default]

  - id: helper-calls-directory
    actions: [tool.call]
    applications: [helper]
    resources: ["directory/*"]
    max_classification: confidential

    The registry lists the server and pins each tool's input schema. After you change a tool's arguments on purpose, pin again; a change by accident fails the tests and the deployed agent refuses the tool.

    uv run agentlib registry pin directory
uv run agentlib policy test            # decides tests/policy-samples.yaml
uv run agentlib policy test --opa      # and checks that OPA agrees

  5. Tests, written before the change

    Three layers come generated: the agent with fakes, the agent with its own configuration, and the two services together in one process. Here is the last, which proves the masking rule end to end with no network:

    # tests/test_helper_with_directory.py (excerpt)
async def ask_as(roles, tmp_path, question, *replies) -> str:
    server_config = load_test_config(SERVER_ENV, state_dir=tmp_path / "server")
    agent_config = load_test_config(AGENT_ENV, state_dir=tmp_path / "agent", roles=roles)
    async with ServiceContainer(server_config) as server_services:
        connector = InProcessMcpConnector({SERVER_ID: build_server(server_services)})
        async with ServiceContainer(
            agent_config, scripted_providers(*replies), mcp_connector=connector
        ) as services:
            context = await services.authenticate(None, application=AGENT, thread_id="th-1")
            graph = build_graph(services, await services.mcp_tools(SERVER_ID))
            await answer(graph, services, context, question)
            return last_shown_to_model(services)


async def test_an_analyst_sees_no_email(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    shown = await ask_as(["analyst"], tmp_path, "Who is in payments?",
                         asks_who_is_in("payments"), "Two people.")
    assert shown.startswith('<untrusted_tool_result tool="directory.people_by_team">')
    assert "Cleo Carr" in shown
    assert MASK in shown and "cleo.carr" not in shown

  6. Run it

    uv run agentlib doctor                       # everything each service needs, checked
uv run agentlib run directory                # terminal 1: MCP server on its port
uv run helper "Who is in the payments team?" # terminal 2: one question
uv run agentlib run helper                   # or serve the agent: POST /invoke
curl -s localhost:8000/invoke -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": {"question": "Who is in payments?"}, "thread_id": "demo"}'
curl -sN localhost:8000/invoke/stream -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": {"question": "Who is in payments?"}}'   # each step as it happens
uv run agentlib graph helper                 # the graph as Mermaid
uv run agentlib check                        # what CI runs: lint, format, types, tests, rules

    With the fake model the agent echoes the question; set EAP_MODEL_PROVIDER and EAP_MODEL_ID in agents/helper/.env for a real one. Change the roles in EAP_IDENTITY_OPTIONS to ["manager"] and the email column appears. Each service writes its audit trail to .agentlib/audit.jsonl.

  7. Ship it

    Nothing in the code changes. The settings do:

    uv run agentlib deploy helper          # first run: writes agents/helper/deploy.env to fill in
uv run agentlib deploy helper --plan   # every adapter, every permission and why
uv run agentlib deploy helper          # writes deploy/helper/: Terraform and a Dockerfile

    See deployment.

When something goes wrong

Every error the library raises says three things: what the code expected, what it got instead, and how to fix it. The entry points a generated service has print it like this, with the line in the library that raised it and the line of your code that led there:

helper: ConfigurationError: the options of provider 'jsonl' are not valid (2 problems)
  expected: path: a path, written as text; only known options: fsync, path, tracing
  got: path = 5; an unknown option 'fsynk' (did you mean 'fsync'?)
  fix: correct the options; the developer guide lists every option with its default
  note: while building the audit adapter 'jsonl', chosen by EAP_AUDIT_PROVIDER with options from EAP_AUDIT_OPTIONS
  raised at: .../ai_agent_lib_core/contracts/options.py:279 in parse_options
  your code: agents/helper/src/helper/__main__.py:21 in _run

Anatomy of an error

PartWhere it comes fromIn code
MessageOne line: what failederror.summary
expected / got / fixSet by the code that raised iterror.expected, error.actual, error.fix, error.facts()
reasonFor a PolicyDenied: the reason code, and the rules that came closest and what each needederror.reason_code
noteContext added on the way up: which adapter, which variable chose it, how many attemptserror.__notes__
caused byThe error underneath, shortened and redactedcauses(error)
raised at / your codeThe traceback: the library's frame and the deepest frame outside the libraryexplain(error)

Raise the same kind of error from your own code: the facts are keyword arguments, and str(error) shows them.

raise ValidationFailed(
    "the input is not a question",
    expected='an object such as {"question": "Say hello to Ada."}',
    actual="no non-empty 'question' in it",
)

In the logs

A logged error becomes fields, so a log search finds every error of one kind and every error whose fix is the same: error_type, error_at, error, error_reason, error_expected, error_actual, error_fix, error_notes, error_causes and error_in_your_code. The HTTP entry points log a refused or failed request with these fields and answer the caller with a code only ({"error": "denied", "reason": "no_matching_rule"}), never the message.

What is never shown

  • Secrets and tokens. Anything shaped like a credential, including a password in a URL, is replaced with [redacted] in messages, logs and output.
  • Caller content. A prompt, a tool argument or a query parameter never enters a message. When it helps to debug, the code puts it in error.detail, which is not part of str(error) and is logged only where shows_details(config) is true: on a developer's machine.
  • A backend's own error text from a database or a cloud API is kept in detail too; the message names its type.

Practices

  • Let entry points report. Generated __main__ and service modules end in return report_error(program, error, details=shows_details(config)): one clear block and exit code 1, with a full traceback for an error that is not the library's.
  • Read the note line first when the message is about an adapter: it names the variable that chose the adapter and the one that holds its options.
  • For a denial, the closest rules are named with what each needed; reproduce it with a sample in tests/policy-samples.yaml and agentlib policy test.
  • A retried call carries the note tried N times, the last error is shown; its audit record has attempts.

Testing spec §17

Because every dependency is injected, every layer is testable with no network and no cloud account. Pick the cheapest layer that can prove the behaviour; most tests belong in the first three rows.

LayerWhat is realTools in ai_agent_lib_core.testing
Your functionsYour codeplain pytest
Agent behaviourYour graph and the pipelines; every port is a fakeFakes, FakeChatModelProvider, calls_tool, structured_reply, FrozenClock, SequentialIds; inspect fakes.model.models[0].calls and fakes.audit.records
Agent as configuredYour .env.example, rules, registry, audit file; only the model is scriptedload_test_config(path, state_dir=, roles=), scripted_providers(*replies), audit_records(), last_shown_to_model()
MCP serverServer, data source over CSV, rules, auditload_test_config(..., test_agent=TEST_AGENT), testing.mcp.call_tool_as(services, server, tool, args, roles=), verify_registration()
REST data sourcesEverything but the HTTP APIrest_stub_providers({"GET /accounts/{id}": {...}})
Services togetherAgent and server in one processtesting.mcp.InProcessMcpConnector
RulesThe rules file, and optionally OPAagentlib policy test [--opa] over tests/policy-samples.yaml
Your own adapterThe adapter against the port's contracttesting.contracts.AuditSinkContract, PolicyDecisionPointContract, DataSourceContract, … (one suite per port)
IntegrationA real OPA, PostgreSQL or AWS accountmark @pytest.mark.integration; opt in with -m integration

Scripting the model

A scripted model replays replies in order. A string is a plain answer; calls_tool(name, **arguments) is the model deciding to call a tool, and structured_reply(Schema, **values) is a structured answer. Name the tool as you registered it, directory.people_by_team or greet: the helper spells it the way the model API sees it.

async def test_the_agent_calls_its_tool_and_answers() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes(model=FakeChatModelProvider([calls_tool("greet", name="Ada"), "I said hello to Ada."]))
    async with fakes.container() as services:
        reply = await ask(services, context(), "Say hello to Ada.")

    assert reply == "I said hello to Ada."
    prompts = fakes.model.models[0].calls
    assert prompts[1][-1].content == frame_untrusted("greet", "Hello, Ada!")
    assert [r.event for r in fakes.audit.records] == ["model.call", "tool.call", "model.call"]

Practices that pay off

  • Test the rules through the agent. The as-configured layer reads .env.example, so a missing rule fails a test, not a demo. Assert on policy_reason_code in audit_records() to prove which rule allowed each step.
  • Test denials as much as successes. Pass roles=[...] to load_test_config or call_tool_as and check the refusal and the masked columns.
  • Never call a real model in unit tests. load_test_config selects the fake model unless you pass fake_model=False. Real-model runs are evals.
  • The network is blocked. Generated workspaces run tests with pytest-socket, allowing only this machine, so an accidental call fails loudly. An eval opts back in with @pytest.mark.enable_socket.
  • Run the gate before you push. agentlib check runs what the generated CI workflow runs (ruff, the format check, mypy, pytest and policy test; add --opa to compare with OPA), and names the step that failed.
  • Pin time and IDs. Use FrozenClock and SequentialIds when an assertion depends on them.
  • Keep the generated tests. They encode the library's contract for your service. agentlib update refreshes them when the library changes.

Structured output for deterministic tests spec §10

Free text is hard to assert on and hard to consume downstream. When a model's answer feeds code (a routing decision, a classification, an extraction), ask for a typed reply. with_structured_output accepts a Pydantic model, a JSON Schema or a StructuredOutput. The model is asked to answer by calling one tool whose parameters are the schema (tool_choice="any"), and the reply is validated inside the model pipeline. A reply that does not match raises ValidationFailed and is audited as failed, so bad output never reaches your code silently.

class Triage(BaseModel):
    """How to route one customer message."""
    category: Literal["billing", "fraud", "other"]
    urgent: bool
    reason: str = Field(max_length=200)


async def triage(services: ServiceContainer, context: RequestContext, text: str) -> Triage:
    model = services.model().with_structured_output(Triage)
    with bind_request_context(context):   # inside a graph node, invocation(context) does this
        return await model.ainvoke(
            [SystemMessage("Classify the customer's message."), HumanMessage(text)]
        )

Tests script the answer with structured_reply: pass an instance of the schema, or the schema and the values, including values the schema would refuse. It names the reply the way the model API sees the schema ({"title": "Account answer"} is offered as Account_answer), so a test never has to.

async def test_a_valid_reply_becomes_a_typed_value() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes(model=FakeChatModelProvider(
        [structured_reply(Triage(category="fraud", urgent=True, reason="card used abroad"))]))
    async with fakes.container() as services:
        result = await triage(services, CALLER, "Someone used my card in Lisbon!")
    assert result == Triage(category="fraud", urgent=True, reason="card used abroad")


async def test_a_reply_outside_the_schema_fails_the_call() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes(model=FakeChatModelProvider([structured_reply(Triage, category="refund", urgent="yes")]))
    async with fakes.container() as services:
        with pytest.raises(ValidationFailed):
            await triage(services, CALLER, "Where is my refund?")
    assert [r.outcome.value for r in fakes.audit.records] == ["failed"]
  • Keep schemas small and closed: Literal for categories, bounds on strings and numbers. The schema is the contract between the model and your code.
  • Put routing decisions in structured nodes and keep free text for the final answer to the person. Graph edges then branch on typed values that tests control exactly.
  • The same schema becomes your eval scorer: an exact match on category is a metric, as the next chapters show.
  • Use include_raw=True when you also need the raw message, for example to log token usage.

Observability with OpenTelemetry

The library separates two records with different readers. The audit trail answers "who did what, and which rule allowed it" for compliance; it is fail-closed and goes to the audit adapter. Operational signals (logs, traces, metrics) answer "is the service healthy and fast" for the people who run it. Neither ever holds prompts, replies, tool arguments, query parameters or tokens.

Signals the library emits

SignalNameAttributesWhen
Log linerequestroute, status, duration_ms, request_idEach POST /invoke to an agent
Log linetool_calltool, outcome (success, tool_error, denied, invalid, failed, error), duration_ms, request_idEach call to an MCP server's tool
Spanagent.invokeagentlib.application, agentlib.request_idEach agent request, once a tracer provider is installed
Spanagent.streamthe sameEach streamed agent request
Spanmcp.tool_call (kind server)agentlib.application, agentlib.tool, agentlib.request_idEach MCP tool call, in the calling agent's trace
Spanchat {model}gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.provider.name, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, agentlib.model_alias, agentlib.outcome, error.typeEach governed model call, a child of the request span
Spanexecute_tool {tool}gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.tool.name, agentlib.read_only, agentlib.mcp_server, agentlib.outcome, agentlib.reason_code, error.typeEach governed tool call
Spanquery {source}.{query}db.operation.name, db.query.summary, agentlib.data_source, agentlib.query, agentlib.classification, agentlib.outcomeEach governed data query
Span eventmodel.call, tool.call, data.query, request.authenticateoutcome plus model_alias/model_provider/model_id, or tool/read_only/mcp_server, or data_source/queryEach governed call, when telemetry is on
Counteragentlib.eventsevent, outcome and the same labelsWhen telemetry is on
Histogramagentlib.duration (s)sameWhen telemetry is on

Every log line also carries time, level, logger, message and service, and inside a request request_id and application. Anything shaped like a credential is replaced with [redacted]; other libraries' loggers are quiet below WARNING. The library's own lines carry metadata only; a message or field your code logs is written as you wrote it, so keep caller content out of it. An error is logged with its facts as fields (error_expected, error_actual, error_fix and the rest; see when something goes wrong). Spans record an error's type, never its message: the request spans do not attach the exception, so no caller content reaches the trace.

Set it up in a service

from ai_agent_lib_core.observability import configure_logging, start_telemetry

def main() -> int:
    configure_logging(APPLICATION)                          # first: JSON lines on stdout
    stop_telemetry = start_telemetry(APPLICATION, config)   # OTLP to the collector when EAP_TELEMETRY is on
    try:
        asyncio.run(_serve(host, port))
    finally:
        stop_telemetry()                                    # flush the last spans and metrics
# the service's environment
EAP_TELEMETRY=opentelemetry                             # spans per call, events and metrics
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318      # the sidecar collector
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=deployment.environment=prod,service.version=1.4.0

Generated services already do this. start_telemetry does nothing when the settings leave telemetry off, and calls configure_telemetry when they turn it on, which needs the otel extra (generated services depend on it). The service name you pass becomes service.name and wins over OTEL_SERVICE_NAME; every other exporter setting is a standard OTEL_ variable read by the SDK. In tests pass span_exporter=InMemorySpanExporter() and a metric_reader to assert on spans without a collector.

Practices

  • Correlate by request_id. The agent sends it to MCP servers with each call, and it appears in the agent's and the server's audit records, log lines and spans. Send x-request-id from your caller to join the chain from the edge.
  • Turn telemetry on in dev and prod with EAP_TELEMETRY=opentelemetry. It is off by default so unit tests stay silent. (The older audit option tracing still turns it on.) In tests, RecordingTelemetry records spans so you can assert on them.
  • Alert on outcomes, not on text. Useful first alerts: agentlib.events{outcome="denied"} rising (a rules change or an attack), outcome="failed" on model.call (structured output or provider errors), agentlib.duration p95 per model_alias.
  • Cost. Model audit records carry input_tokens and output_tokens with tenant, subject and application; aggregate them from the audit stream for cost attribution.
  • Keep content out. If you need prompts and replies for debugging or evals, store them deliberately, classified and with retention, in a store you own. Do not add them to log lines or span attributes.

One trace from the edge to the data. The agent's MCP client puts the W3C traceparent of the current span in each call's metadata, and the server continues that trace, so a backend shows the request, its model and tool calls, the MCP call and the server's query as one tree. Span names and attributes follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.

Evals, offline and online spec concern 10

Unit tests prove the plumbing with a scripted model. Evals measure the behaviour of the real model on your task. ai_agent_lib_core.evaluation holds the pieces, off the request path (an import rule keeps it there), and every generated agent comes with an eval ready to run.

Offline: a dataset, a scorer, a bar

Cases are JSON lines next to the service: an id, the input, what a good answer has in expected, and optional tags. Lines starting with # are comments.

# agents/support/evals/triage.jsonl
{"id": "card-abroad", "input": {"text": "Someone used my card in Lisbon, I'm in Leeds!"}, "expected": {"category": "fraud", "urgent": true}}
{"id": "double-charge", "input": {"text": "Why was I charged twice for March?"}, "expected": {"category": "billing", "urgent": false}, "tags": ["billing"]}

Score with the same structured schema the code uses, so most metrics are exact matches rather than opinions:

from ai_agent_lib_core.evaluation import exact, judged, load_cases, run_eval, scored_by
from ai_agent_lib_core.testing import load_eval_config


@pytest.mark.eval
@pytest.mark.enable_socket                                  # the network is blocked for other tests
async def test_triage_meets_its_bar(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = load_eval_config(SERVICE / ".env", state_dir=tmp_path)   # keeps the real model
    if config.model.provider == "fake":
        pytest.skip("set a real model in .env to run evals")
    async with ServiceContainer(config) as services:
        context = await services.authenticate(None, application=APPLICATION, thread_id="eval")
        report = await run_eval(
            lambda case: triage(services, context, case.input["text"]),
            load_cases(SERVICE / "evals" / "triage.jsonl"),
            [exact("category"), exact("urgent")],
            concurrency=4,
        )
    print("\n".join(report.summary()))
    report.require({"category": 0.90, "urgent": 0.85})

report.require fails with the metric, the bar and the score (expected: category >= 0.90, then the score it got) and names the cases below it. report.by_tag breaks the scores down by tag, and report.to_json() is the record to keep with the change.

uv run agentlib eval support      # before merging a prompt, model or rule change
uv run agentlib eval              # every service
  • Gate changes on evals. Run them when a prompt, model alias, tool description or rule changes, and keep the report with the commit.
  • Test the scorer itself with a scripted model, so a broken scorer cannot pass silently: run_eval runs unchanged on Fakes.
  • Use a judge only for what cannot be matched. For tone or faithfulness, add a judge alias in EAP_MODEL_ALIASES and score with judged(services.model("judge").with_structured_output(Verdict).ainvoke, "Is the answer faithful to the sources?", name="faithful"). Calibrate the judge on a hand-labelled sample first. scored_by(name, function) takes any function of the case and the output.
  • Evals are governed calls too. They go through policy and audit, so the eval identity needs rules for model.route on the aliases it uses.

Online: measure production without reading it

Production evals must respect the same rule as everything else: content stays out of logs and audit. What you can measure today without any content:

SignalSourceWhat it tells you
Structured-output failure rateagentlib.events{event="model.call", outcome="failed"}The model is drifting from the schema.
Denial rate by reasonaudit reason_codeUsers asking for what they may not have, or a rules regression.
Guardrail findingsaudit guardrail_* attributesPersonal data or injection attempts reaching the model.
Tool error ratetool_call log lines, outcomeThe model calls tools badly, or a backend is failing.
Steps and tokens per requestaudit records grouped by request_idLoops, verbosity, cost per answer.
Latency per aliasagentlib.durationProvider slowdowns; when to move a node to fast.

For quality scores on real conversations, run an eval worker off the request path: the application writes a sample of conversations (with consent and a retention period, classified like the data in them) to a store it owns; a scheduled job scores them with the offline scorer and the judge alias, and emits the scores as metrics labelled by application and model alias, joined to traces by request_id. Use the scorers from ai_agent_lib_core.evaluation in that job, so offline and online share one definition.

Security and governance practices spec §9, §12–13

  • Every service has its own identity. Register each agent and MCP server as an application at the identity provider. The agent's token audience is its own API; the server's audience in the registry matches the server's jwt options. Turn on accept_service_tokens only for services that are called without a user.
  • Delegate, never forward. Configure exchange on agents that call MCP servers. The server then sees the user and the agent in one token, and rules can require both (roles and agents in the same rule).
  • Write narrow rules. One application per rule, explicit resources, a max_classification. Prefer obligations (mask_columns, max_rows) to a second, broader tool. Keep tests/policy-samples.yaml covering every rule, including the denials, and run agentlib policy test --opa in CI so the two engines agree.
  • Classify data at the query. Each named query declares its classification; the registry and the agent entry declare ceilings. A request above the ceiling is refused before any data moves.
  • Treat tool results as untrusted. Framing is on by default (frame_tool_results); keep it on. Set guardrail injection and pii to block for tools that read user-generated content.
  • Pin every tool. Production servers verify their pins at startup (verify_registration(..., require_pins=True) outside local); agents refuse a tool whose schema drifted.
  • Secrets by name. Options hold secret names (auth_secret, client_secret), the secrets adapter holds values. Scope the task role to the service's Secrets Manager prefix.
  • TLS everywhere. HTTP adapters refuse plain http:// to a remote host unless allow_http is set; use ca_file for a private CA rather than turning verification off (there is no switch for that).
  • Never deploy as local. Set EAP_DEPLOYMENT_ENV in every task definition; the guard refuses development adapters there, and managed runtimes must name it.

Deployment on AWS Fargate spec §16

Each agent and each MCP server is one Fargate service. agentlib deploy derives what it needs from the settings it will run with, and writes the Terraform and the Dockerfiles; you read the plan and run terraform yourself. Nothing is applied for you and nothing calls AWS.

uv run agentlib deploy helper          # first run: writes agents/helper/deploy.env with example values
uv run agentlib deploy helper --plan   # adapters, permissions and why, sidecars, warnings
uv run agentlib deploy helper          # writes deploy/helper/ and deploy/modules/agentlib-service/

docker build -f deploy/helper/Dockerfile -t helper .
docker build -f deploy/opa/Dockerfile -t helper-opa .      # when the plan lists the OPA sidecar
cd deploy/helper && terraform init && terraform plan

Settings, not hand-written policy

deploy.env holds the EAP_ settings of the deployed service. Its values become the task's environment, so it may hold no secret: a secret variable in it stops the command, naming the variable and never its value. Settings for a developer's machine (EAP_DEPLOYMENT_ENV=local) and local-only adapters are refused too. An adapter that comes from ai-agent-lib-aws needs that distribution, with the adapter's extra (bedrock, postgres), in the service's own dependencies; telemetry needs the core otel extra. The plan names each requirement to add.

Each adapter declares, from its own options, the IAM actions it calls and the resources it calls them on. The plan lists them with the reason for each, and permissions.tf holds exactly those statements. Where a resource cannot be narrowed from the settings, such as an ID AWS assigns, the plan and the file carry a check: line. For the starting deploy.env of an agent and one Redshift data source, the adapters ask for:

AdapterActionsResourcesWhy
model bedrockbedrock:InvokeModel
bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream		arn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account}:inference-profile/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0
arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0		call the configured models
model bedrockbedrock:GetInferenceProfilearn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account}:inference-profile/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0find the model behind an inference profile
secrets secrets_managersecretsmanager:GetSecretValuearn:aws:secretsmanager:{region}:{account}:secret:eap/helper/*read the service's secrets
audit firehosefirehose:PutRecord
firehose:DescribeDeliveryStream		arn:aws:firehose:{region}:{account}:deliverystream/eap-auditwrite audit records, and check at startup that the stream is active
checkpoint postgresrds-db:connectarn:aws:rds-db:{region}:{account}:dbuser:*/helpersign in to the checkpoint database as the configured user
check: replace * with the resource ID of the database cluster or instance (it starts with cluster- or db-)
registry s3_files3:GetObjectarn:aws:s3:::my-eap-registry/registry/agents.yaml
arn:aws:s3:::my-eap-registry/registry/mcp-tools.yaml		read the agent and MCP tool registries
guardrails bedrockbedrock:ApplyGuardrailarn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account}:guardrail/abc123def456check content with the configured guardrail
data source ledger (redshift_data)redshift-data:ExecuteStatementarn:aws:redshift-serverless:{region}:{account}:workgroup/*run the queries of data source ledger
check: a workgroup's ARN holds its ID, not its name; replace * with the ID of workgroup analytics
data source ledger (redshift_data)redshift-serverless:GetCredentialsarn:aws:redshift-serverless:{region}:{account}:workgroup/*sign in to the workgroup as the service's role
check: a workgroup's ARN holds its ID, not its name; replace * with the ID of workgroup analytics
data source ledger (redshift_data)redshift-data:DescribeStatement
redshift-data:GetStatementResult
redshift-data:CancelStatement		*wait for a query, read its rows, and stop it at its deadline
check: these actions take no resource; AWS lets a caller see only its own statements

{region} and {account} become the deployment's region and account in permissions.tf. An adapter of your own declares its needs with ServiceProviders.register(..., access=rule); one that does not is named in the plan, so nothing is granted silently.

What is written

FileWhoseWhat it holds
deploy/helper/settings.tfagentlib's, rewritten each runThe command, the port, the environment from deploy.env, and which sidecars run
deploy/helper/permissions.tfagentlib's, rewritten each runOne IAM statement per declared access, with its reason as a comment
deploy/helper/main.tf, variables.tf, Dockerfile, README.md, terraform.tfvars.exampleyours, written onceThe root module calling the reference module; the image build
deploy/modules/agentlib-service/agentlib's, rewritten each runThe reference module, with tests that run against a mocked AWS provider
deploy/opa/agentlib's, rewritten each runThe OPA sidecar's Dockerfile and the platform's Rego bundle

The task

ContainerRoleNotes
serviceYour agent or MCP serverRuns helper-serve or the server's command on its port. Health check on /healthz; point the load balancer at /readyz, which turns true after services.validate() passes. SIGTERM stops new requests and lets calls in flight finish.
volume-initMakes /tmp writable, then exitsRuns before the service starts (the service waits for it to succeed); not essential.
opaPolicy decisions on the task's loopback addressWhen the settings select the opa adapter on localhost. The image holds the platform bundle and your policies/ folder.
collectorReceives OTLP on localhost:4318When EAP_TELEMETRY=opentelemetry. Sends traces to X-Ray and metrics to CloudWatch; not essential, so the service keeps running without it.
  • Every container has a read-only root file system; /tmp is the writable place. The service runs as a user with no rights over its own code. Tasks get no public IP.
  • The execution role can pull images and write this service's log group, nothing else. The task role holds the declared statements, plus the collector's when it runs.
  • A deployment that fails its health checks rolls back on its own (the ECS circuit breaker).
  • The module does not make the cluster, the network, the load balancer, the image repositories, the secrets, or the AWS resources the adapters use: those belong to the platform.
  • An image build installs the library from a package index; a workspace that uses a local checkout gets a warning in the plan.

What is built, and what is not yet

So you can plan around it: the specification is wider than the code. Everything in the first column is implemented and tested (about 1,600 offline tests); the second column is specified only.

BuiltSpecified, not built
Configuration, profiles, mixing, one-way guard, config explain, config options with JSON Schema, the telemetry switch, limitsRuntime policy bundles
Container, provider registry, provider packs, doctor, SyncServices—
Model pipeline: audit, identity, policy, guardrails, structured output, timeouts and retries, budgets per requestPer-tenant budgets and the pause switch, context bounding
Tool pipeline: audit, registry and pins, policy, guardrails, framing, retries for read-only toolsHuman approval, idempotency keys, runtime judges
Identity: static development tokens, JWT with Entra preset, on-behalf-of and RFC 8693 exchange—
Policy: rules engine and OPA, with obligations; denials that name the closest rules; policy testagent.call, skill.activate, memory.* actions in practice
Data: DuckDB over CSV, REST, Redshift Data API; catalogue readersRedshift driver option
State: SQLite and Postgres checkpointers, scoped threadsLong-term memory, cache, erasure, state schema versioning
MCP server middleware and client with token exchange and trace propagationTeam router
HTTP entry point, health, readiness, graceful shutdown, streaming of graph stepsToken-by-token streaming
Errors with expected, got and fix; JSON logs with those facts as fields; a span per governed call with GenAI names; events and metrics—
Testing kit, contract suites, scripted-reply helpers, the evaluation packageRelease admission
CLI: init, new, link, pin, doctor, run, graph, policy test, update, config options, check, eval, deploy—
Deployment: the reference Terraform module for Fargate, IAM derived from the adapters—

Developer experience: what changed, and what is next

Writing this guide meant using every surface of the library as a newcomer would. These were the changes that would most shorten the path from "first agent" to "in production", ranked by impact for the effort. Each says what was built and where to read about it.

  1. Errors that say what was expected, what came, and the fix

    Every library error carries expected, got and fix, notes on which adapter and variable were involved, and where it was raised in the library and in your code; logs carry the same facts as fields. See when something goes wrong. Not built: a link to the guide's anchor in each message.

    builterrors, logs

  2. Adapters declare their options model

    Startup checks every adapter's options before building anything and reports every problem at once, with "did you mean". agentlib config options shows them, with --schema for editors, and this guide's option tables come from the code.

    builtconfig, docs, CLI

  3. One-line helpers for scripted replies

    calls_tool("directory.people_by_team", team="payments") and structured_reply(Triage, category="fraud") spell names the way the model API sees them. See testing.

    builttesting

  4. An eval kit and agentlib eval

    Cases, scorers, a report with bars, load_eval_config, the eval marker in generated workspaces, and an eval in every new agent. See evals.

    builtevaluation, CLI

  5. First-class traces

    A span per model, tool and query call with GenAI names, trace context carried to MCP servers, and EAP_TELEMETRY. See observability.

    builtobservability

  6. Defaults live in the binding table

    config explain, docs/variables.md, .env.example and this guide show the same defaults from one place.

    builtconfig, docs

  7. Hardened workspaces and CI templates

    Sockets blocked in tests, the integration and eval markers, a CI workflow for Linux and Windows, and agentlib check to run the same gate locally.

    builtCLI, templates

  8. Resilience and budgets

    Timeouts per attempt, retries with backoff for transient errors, and call and token budgets per request, all in EAP_LIMITS. Not built: budgets per tenant and the pause switch.

    built in partpipeline

  9. Streaming responses

    POST /invoke/stream sends each graph step as a server-sent event, through the same pipelines. Not built: streaming the model's tokens one by one.

    built in partintegrations

  10. A deployment path

    The reference Terraform module for Fargate with the OPA and collector sidecars, IAM derived from the adapters, and agentlib deploy --plan. See deployment.

    builtdeploy

  11. Smaller cleanups

    EAP_RUNTIME_POLICY is gone until it does something; the sync facade is SyncServices; the public API is listed in the reference. Not done: widening the type of Fakes.telemetry.

    built in partvarious

Reference

Everything in this chapter is generated from the code when the guide is built, so it matches the version you have. Defaults shown for section adapters come from resolving an empty configuration under each profile.

Environment variables owned by the library

Set them in the service's .env locally, or in the task definition when deployed. The environment wins over .env. An unknown EAP_ name stops startup.

VariablePurposeDefaultNotes
EAP_PROFILEDefault adapter set: local or aws.
Chooses the whole default adapter set in one word. local runs with no cloud account: files, SQLite, an in-process rules engine and a development identity. aws selects the managed adapters. A profile only supplies defaults; any section can still name another adapter.
local
EAP_DEPLOYMENT_ENVWhere the process runs: local, dev or prod. Drives the one-way guard.
Says where the process runs. Anything other than local turns on the one-way guard: adapters registered as local only (the development identity, the rules engine, JSONL audit, SQLite, DuckDB over CSV, the fake model) refuse to start. Inside ECS, Fargate or Lambda the value must be dev or prod.
local
EAP_TELEMETRYOperational traces and metrics: off or opentelemetry.
With opentelemetry every governed call is a span named after the GenAI conventions, and the agentlib.events and agentlib.duration metrics are recorded, through the OpenTelemetry API. The service sends them by calling configure_telemetry(); where to is set with the standard OTEL_ variables. The audit option tracing: true also turns it on.
off
EAP_LIMITSJSON timeouts, retries and budgets of governed calls.
Keys model and tool, each with timeout_seconds, retries, backoff_seconds and max_backoff_seconds, and budget with model_calls, tool_calls and tokens per request. Only transient failures are tried again, and a tool only when it only reads. A request over its budget stops with BudgetExceeded. agentlib config options limits lists every key.
model: 120 s, 2 retries; tool: 60 s, 1 retry; budget: 50 model calls and 100 tool calls per requestJSON
EAP_TLS_CA_BUNDLEEnterprise CA file for the AWS clients, such as the Bedrock model client.
Path to the enterprise CA bundle that the AWS clients trust, for networks that inspect TLS. It applies to the Bedrock model client and the other boto3 clients only; HTTP adapters take their own ca_file option.
not set
EAP_MODEL_PROVIDERProvider of the default model alias.
The provider of the model behind the default alias, and of any alias that does not name its own provider.
local: anthropic, aws: bedrock
EAP_MODEL_IDModel behind the default alias.
The model ID behind the default alias, as the provider spells it. Until it is set, services.model() raises a ConfigurationError that says to set it. A service with no model, such as an MCP server, leaves it unset.
not set: required before services.model()
EAP_MODEL_ALIASESJSON map of further aliases, e.g. {"fast": {"model_id": "..."}}.
Further aliases, so code asks for a role (fast, judge) rather than a model. A value is a model ID or an object with model_id and an optional provider.
{}: only the default aliasJSON
EAP_SECRETS_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the secrets section.
Where adapters get credentials by name. Adapters: env, secrets_manager.
local: env, aws: secrets_manager
EAP_SECRETS_OPTIONSJSON options for the secrets adapter.
Options of the selected secrets adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options secrets lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_AUDIT_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the audit section.
Where the audit trail of every governed call goes. Adapters: firehose, jsonl.
local: jsonl, aws: firehose
EAP_AUDIT_OPTIONSJSON options for the audit adapter.
Options of the selected audit adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options audit lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_IDENTITY_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the identity section.
Who the caller is: a development identity locally, OAuth 2.0 JWTs when deployed. Adapters: jwt, static.
local: static, aws: jwt
EAP_IDENTITY_OPTIONSJSON options for the identity adapter.
Options of the selected identity adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options identity lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_CHECKPOINT_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the checkpoint section.
Where LangGraph keeps conversation state between turns. Adapters: none, postgres, sqlite.
local: sqlite, aws: postgres
EAP_CHECKPOINT_OPTIONSJSON options for the checkpoint adapter.
Options of the selected checkpoint adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options checkpoint lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_REGISTRY_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the registry section.
The agent and MCP tool registries. Adapters: file, s3_file.
local: file, aws: s3_file
EAP_REGISTRY_OPTIONSJSON options for the registry adapter.
Options of the selected registry adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options registry lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_POLICY_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the policy section.
Who may do what: the in-process rules engine locally, OPA when deployed. Adapters: opa, rules.
local: rules, aws: opa
EAP_POLICY_OPTIONSJSON options for the policy adapter.
Options of the selected policy adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options policy lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_GUARDRAILS_PROVIDERAdapter that serves the guardrails section.
Content checks on prompts, replies and tool results. Adapters: bedrock, patterns.
local: patterns, aws: bedrock
EAP_GUARDRAILS_OPTIONSJSON options for the guardrails adapter.
Options of the selected guardrails adapter, as one JSON object. Unknown keys stop startup. agentlib config options guardrails lists each adapter's options. See adapter options.
{}: the adapter's defaultsJSON
EAP_DATA_SOURCESJSON map of named data sources, e.g. {"accounts": {"kind": "duckdb_csv", "data_dir": "data", "queries_dir": "queries"}}.
Named data sources for MCP tools. Each entry names its adapter with kind; the other keys are that adapter's options. Code asks for services.data_source("ledger") and never sees the backend.
{}: no data sourcesJSON
EAP_SECRET_<NAME>One named secret for the env secrets adapter.
EAP_SECRET_RATES_TOKEN supplies the secret rates_token. Options such as auth_secret name the secret, never the value.
not setsensitive

Variables that belong to other tools

These keep their own names. The library reads them and never renames them.

VariablePurposeDefaultNotes
AWS_PROFILEAWS named profile, for example one signed in through SSO.
Read by the AWS session for local runs, for example after aws sso login.
not set
AWS_REGIONAWS region.
Region of every AWS client the library builds.
not setalso AWS_DEFAULT_REGION
AWS_CA_BUNDLECA file for AWS clients.
The AWS SDK's own CA setting, honoured as boto3 does.
not set
AWS_EXECUTION_ENVSet by AWS inside ECS, Fargate and Lambda. A process that has it must name its deployment environment as dev or prod.
Set by AWS on its managed runtimes. Its presence with EAP_DEPLOYMENT_ENV=local stops startup, so a container never runs with development adapters by accident.
not set
HTTPS_PROXYOutbound proxy.
Outbound proxy. The AWS clients and the anthropic model use it; the jwt identity provider and rest data sources use it only when their use_proxy option is set. Masked wherever it is shown, since it can carry credentials.
not setsensitive also https_proxy
NO_PROXYHosts that bypass the proxy.
Comma-separated hosts the AWS clients reach without the proxy.
not setalso no_proxy
ANTHROPIC_API_KEYAPI key for the anthropic model provider.
Supplies the secret anthropic_api_key, which the anthropic model provider asks the secrets port for. Masked wherever it is shown.
not setsensitive

Read by the OpenTelemetry SDK once configure_telemetry() has installed it; the library never reads them itself. Defaults are the SDK's.

VariablePurposeSDK default
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINTBase address of the collector. Traces go to /v1/traces and metrics to /v1/metrics.http://localhost:4318
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINTFull traces address, when traces go somewhere else.not set
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINTFull metrics address, when metrics go somewhere else.not set
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERSHeaders for every export, such as a vendor key. Keep it in the task's secrets.not set
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATECA file for a collector behind enterprise TLS.not set
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTESExtra resource attributes, e.g. deployment.environment=prod,service.version=1.4.0.not set
OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVALMilliseconds between metric exports.60000
OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAYMilliseconds the batch span processor waits before sending.5000
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLERSampling. Use parentbased_traceidratio with OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG for high volume.parentbased_always_on
OTEL_SDK_DISABLEDTurns the SDK off without a code change.false

Adapter options

The keys each adapter accepts in its EAP_<SECTION>_OPTIONS object, or beside "kind" in a data source. Unknown keys stop startup. Relative paths resolve against the folder of the .env file.

model · anthropic

No options. The key is the secret anthropic_api_key: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY with the env secrets adapter, Secrets Manager when deployed. Uses HTTPS_PROXY. Needs the anthropic extra.

model · bedrock

No options. Uses the AWS session settings (AWS_PROFILE, AWS_REGION) and EAP_TLS_CA_BUNDLE.

model · fake local only

No options. Echoes the question as fake: <question>; tests script its replies.

secrets · env

No options. Serves each secret from a EAP_SECRET_<NAME> variable.

secrets · secrets_manager

Options of the secrets_manager secrets provider. (SecretsManagerOptions)

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
prefixtext""Put before a secret's name to form its ID in Secrets Manager, for example eap/accounts-agent/. It keeps one service's secrets apart from another's, and an IAM policy can be scoped to it.
cache_secondsnumber300.0How long a secret is kept before it is read again, so that a rotated secret is picked up without a restart. 0 reads it every time.

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning

fsynctrue | falsetrueForce each record to disk before write returns.

identity · jwt

Options of the jwt identity provider. (JwtIdentityOptions)

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
preset"entra"not setentra fills in the issuer, key location, token endpoint and claim names for Microsoft Entra ID from tenant_id.

algorithmslist of "RS256" | "RS384" | "RS512" | "PS256" | "PS384" | "PS512" | "ES256" | "ES384" | "ES512" | "EdDSA"["RS256"]The signature algorithms to accept. Only asymmetric ones exist here.
claimsobject of text{}Claim names that differ from the preset, by what they supply: subject, tenant, roles, actor, scopes, kind.
tenanttextnot setThe tenant every caller belongs to, when tokens carry no tenant claim.
required_scopeslist of text[]Delegated scopes a user's token must all carry.
accept_service_tokenstrue | falsefalseAccept tokens an application obtained for itself, with no user. Refused unless this is set.
service_tokens_are"kind_claim" | "without_scopes" | "actor_is_subject"not setHow an application's own token is told from a user's. Required without a preset, because issuers differ and a wrong guess would let an application act as a user.

leeway_secondsinteger60Clock difference tolerated when checking validity.
jwks_cache_secondsinteger86400How long the signing keys are kept before they are read again.
timeout_secondsnumber5.0How long reading the signing keys may take.

exchange.kind"on_behalf_of" | "token_exchange"not seton_behalf_of is the JWT bearer grant as Microsoft Entra ID implements delegation. token_exchange is RFC 8693. The default follows the preset.

CLI commands and flags

Every command takes --workspace where it acts on a workspace; run agentlib COMMAND --help for the same text.

agentlib check

Run what CI runs: lint, format, types, tests and the policy samples.

agentlib check [OPTIONS]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--opaoffAlso check that OPA agrees with the rules.
--keep-goingoffRun every check even after one fails.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib config explain

Show every setting of SERVICE and where it came from. Secrets are masked.

agentlib config explain [OPTIONS] SERVICE
FlagDefaultMeaning
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib config options

List the adapters of each PORT, or the options of the adapter NAME with their defaults.

agentlib config options [OPTIONS] [PORT] [NAME]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--schemaoffPrint the adapter's options as JSON Schema, for an editor.

agentlib deploy

Write the Terraform and Dockerfiles that run SERVICE on ECS Fargate.

agentlib deploy [OPTIONS] SERVICE

--bundlenoneThe platform's Rego bundle, for the OPA sidecar. Default: the library checkout's.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

FlagDefaultMeaning

Print the graph of AGENT as a Mermaid diagram.

agentlib registry pin

Pin the input schema of every tool of the MCP server SERVER.

agentlib registry pin [OPTIONS] SERVER
FlagDefaultMeaning
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib run

Start SERVICE and keep it running: an agent's HTTP entry point, or an MCP server.

agentlib run [OPTIONS] SERVICE [ARGUMENTS...]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib update

Bring generated files up to what this version of agentlib writes.

agentlib update [OPTIONS]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--diffoffShow what would change in files you changed.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

Service entry points

What agentlib new generates for each service. Configuration stays in variables; these flags only say where to listen.

CommandFlagDefaultMeaning
<agent> QUESTION--threaddefaultAsk one question from the command line, continuing this conversation.
<agent>-serve--host127.0.0.1Address to listen on. Use 0.0.0.0 in a container.
<agent>-serve--portthe port chosen at generation (8000 for the first agent)Port of POST /invoke, /healthz and /readyz.
<mcp server>--host127.0.0.1Address to listen on.
<mcp server>--portthe port chosen at generation (8100 for the first server)Port of the Streamable HTTP endpoint /mcp and the health routes.

POST /invoke takes {"input": ..., "thread_id": "..."} with Authorization: Bearer <token> and an optional x-request-id, and answers {"output": ..., "thread_id": ..., "request_id": ...}.

Errors

Every error the library raises is an AgentLibError. Catch the type, never parse the message; read expected, actual and fix as fields (see when something goes wrong). The HTTP entry point maps them to a status and a code; the error's own text never reaches the caller.

ErrorMeansHTTPRetry?
ConfigurationErrorConfiguration is invalid or missing. Raised at startup.—No: fix the configuration
PolicyDeniedPolicy, an entitlement or a guardrail refused. Carries reason_code. At sign-in it becomes 401.403 deniedNever
ValidationFailedStructured output or a schema check failed.400 invalidOnly with a changed prompt
TransientErrorThrottling, a timeout or a server error that may clear. The pipelines have already tried again as EAP_LIMITS allows.503 unavailable + retry-afterYes, with backoff
IntegrityErrorThe audit record could not be written, or a hash or pin did not match.500 internalNo: page someone
CredentialsExpiredErrorA sign-in session or token expired, for example the developer's AWS SSO session.500 internalAfter signing in again
BudgetExceededThe request reached its model call, tool call or token budget in EAP_LIMITS.429 budget_exceededLater
ExecutionPausedThe pause switch is set. Reserved.409 pausedAfter it is lifted
